explanation: Generate enough independent fair bits to cover the inclusive interval, rejecting unused bit patterns. Keep the outcome count and zero-based offsets in unsigned 64-bit integers, supporting all 2^32 signed-int outcomes. The driver retains 100000 samples per attempt and five retries. Marginal, pair and triple checks retain tolerance 0.01 and their expected/complement count thresholds of 50 before narrowing. A sliding frequency map computes exactly the original birthday-window predicate in expected linear time, including its omitted final window, minimum 1000 possible windows and 0.4 threshold.
timeComplexity: O(log(R+1)) expected fair-bit draws per generated value for interval size R. A complete N=100000 sample attempt uses expected O(N log(R+1)) total time, including expected O(N) statistical checking; the driver preserves up to five full attempts.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space for the sampler. The full statistical driver uses O(N) sample and sliding-window storage.
attribution: Original EPI Practice C++ implementation, independently authored from the public EPI problem contract and the repository-authored C# algorithm. Uses unchanged local EPI Judge serialization and test framework APIs; upstream reference sources are not modified.
